Higher animals are social and will therefore first try to find out whether you are something to play with or something to eat. If you know them a little, you can use that to get friends with them, or to make them uninterested in you.

Most animals can easily be controlled by inflicting a little pain on them - punch on the nose, going for their eyes, and so on. Even if you don't land a knockout punch, they will often give up - though some animals will grow more aggressive if you fight back.

We usually know very well how most animals attack, and we can usually react accordingly to avoid their blows. That alone is often enough to make animals loose interest in us.

Running away is not an option with most animals of comparable size - they outsprint us, and their hunting instinct gets triggered from our running.

All in all, a normal human who knows a little about animals and doesn't panic should be able to deal with any animal out there easily - and most of us have probably already done so more or less w/o realising when we calmed down a dog, avoided a bear or such in an area where they roam freely, and so on. And even if it comes to a fight, we should actually win, despite their superior claws and teeth, but as it's difficult to stay calm or focus your fear productively in such a situation, the ratio is actually lower. If we are unprepared and attacked by surprise, we have no chance - as has been shown repeatedly in areas where lions, tigers, or other dangerous animals have hunted humans.
